analysis: Reviewed ClusterOnboardingLive.swift head 1-889. The PR threads a ClusterServingScope through the forwarded control path. planModels (head 600-601) sends context.settings.servingScope in the forwarded request. The leader's executeForwarded passes request.scope into localPlanModels (head 272) and localAdopt (head 276). The new planningScope (head 609-611) picks scope in this order: forwarded scope, then local setting, then saved leadership.scope, then .publicServing. The plan uses this only to set coordinator: !isLocalOnly (head 633). Forwarded commands come only from the pinned paired Mac, checked in forwardReply (head 228-232). That peer could already set scope through the existing .scope op (head 284-286 -> localSetScope). Letting it name scope for planning and adopt therefore adds no new privilege over the existing forwarded set. The fallback default to .publicServing when nothing is saved existed before in the leadership path; nothing shows a new public-exposure default. Private image qualification still refuses forwarding (head 214-215). It also still labels public traffic as prohibited for the private candidate (head 672-673). Open integration question: localAdopt(scope:) is not in these units. The next pass should verify that a forwarded scope applies only to that adopt and does not persist. It should also check that a forwarded scope cannot bypass qualification or public-serving authorization gates on the coordinator, which remain authoritative (TB-011, T-052, T-054). No cache, attestation or encryption paths (T-041, TB-002) are touched here. The scope is coordinator-side routing policy that the provider does not enforce.
